## Definitions and Theorems

<!-- 
::: {#def-expectation}
## Expectation
For a random variable $X$ with density $f(x)$, the expectation is defined as

$$
\E[X] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x f(x)\, dx
$$ {#eq-expectation}
:::

::: {#lem-linear-integral}
For integrable $g, h$ and constants $a, b$,
$\int (a g + b h) = a \int g + b \int h$.
:::

::: {#thm-linearity}
## Linearity of Expectation
For any constants $a, b$, $\E[aX + b] = a\E[X] + b$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Follows from @eq-expectation and @lem-linear-integral.
:::

::: {#cor-centered}
$\E[X - \E[X]] = 0$.
:::

::: {.remark}
@thm-linearity does not require independence; compare with $\Var(X + Y) = \Var(X) + \Var(Y) + 2\Cov(X, Y)$.
:::

## Examples

::: {#exm-normal}
If $X_1, \dots, X_n \iid N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, then $\E[\bar X] = \mu$ and
$\hat\mu_{\text{MLE}} = \argmax_\mu \ell(\mu) = \bar X$.
:::
